Ideally, we'd want to expand the wildcard before we decide the `return_scalar`, but we don't have the schema information of the plan here. Is there a good way we can do something like rewriting projection here?

Not expanding it at least shouldn't raise. Anyway, I decided to fix this first and think about optimizations later. 

This fixes #13809.

### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

pl.DataFrame({"A":["B"]}).select(pl.all().is_in(["C"]))
# segmentation fault
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

It seems to be specific to `pl.all`

```python
pl.DataFrame({"A":["B"]}).select(pl.first().is_in(["C"]))
# shape: (1, 1)
# ┌───────┐
# │ A     │
# │ ---   │
# │ bool  │
# ╞═══════╡
# │ false │
# └───────┘
```

It looks like this behaviour started in `0.20.1`

No segfault.

This may be related to the fact that `is_in` does not work on multiple columns simultaneously:

```python
pl.DataFrame({
    "a": [1],
    "b": [1],
}).select(pl.col("a", "b").is_in([1]))
```
```
pyo3_runtime.PanicException: expr col("a").is_in([Series]) is not implemented correctly. 'returns_scalar' and 'elementwise' are mutually exclusive
```
Not a segfault but perhaps this error is causing a segfault.

Ok, it's related but not the exact same path. For anyone (@orlp?) who is much better at this than I, the issue in both instances involves the `returns_scalar` element. In PR #13091 a while back we updated the `returns_scalar` calculation for `is_in`. It appears to fail when broadcasting to multiple columns, but I'm not sure how to properly deal with it (should it be false or true?).

In the `pl.col("a", "b")` case, the `returns_scalar` value is messing things up. In the `pl.all()`, case, I think [this line](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-plan/src/utils.rs#L155) is hitting an infinitely recursive loop that overflows the stack frame and causes the segfault.
